summary: Prolonged chat warmup delay and elevated TTFB after compatibility-layer upgrade
description:
Issue summary:
LumineAI reports a sustained increase in chat session warmup time and higher-than-normal TTFB for streaming chat completions after our compatibility-layer (runtime) upgrade on 2026-03-11. The impact is across their dedicated pool in us-east with spillover errors reported in eu-west.

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat UX shows 2.5–4x higher latency for first token across long-tail sessions.
- Several sessions time out at 30s in regions with heavy cache churn.
- Business impact: session abandonment and automated SLA alerts for LumineAI's enterprise contract.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (customer-dedicated GPU pool) in prod-us-east.
- Runtime roll: compatibility-layer v2.1 deployed 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC.
- Compiler/Kernel bundle: kernels-v3.4 (hot-swap).
- Affected model pins: rw-infer-13b-v2.1-quant and rw-chat-7b-compat.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Create a new chat session with conversation history ~4 turns (approx 250 tokens).
2) Call /v1/chat/completions with streaming enabled and model rw-infer-13b-v2.1-quant.
3) Observe time to first byte/token in response headers and stream.
4) Repeat after a few minutes; warm sessions occasionally show normal latency but many cold sessions take 6–12s to yield the first token.

Logs/metrics attached:
- Pod traces: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rt/serving-traces?var-customer=LumineAI&from=2026-03-11T00:00Z
- Latency histogram (customer): https://metrics.redwood.ai/dashboard/lumineai-ttfb-2026-03-11
comments: 2026-03-12T10:15Z - Support (Ava Martinez): Opened ticket after LumineAI CS reported elevated cold-start warmup times post-upgrade. Customer provided sample request IDs: req_6d9f2a, req_fc3b1c.

2026-03-12T13:02Z - SRE (Ravi Patel): Confirmed TTFB increase in prod-us-east for the customer's pool coincident with compatibility-layer v2.1 rollout. Initial hypothesis: kernel ABI change introduced extra handshake/initialization path for certain model configurations.

2026-03-12T16:40Z - Engineering (Marina Cho): Reproduced locally against kernels-v3.4; observed ~3x slower allocator checkout time and additional 80–150ms per-layer compile overhead for quantized kernels on first inference. Noted higher syscalls during session setup (tls/session resume).

2026-03-13T09:10Z - Support (Ava Martinez): Customer accepted temporary routing to runtime-1.9-stable for critical customers. Provided instructions to LumineAI contact for switching via console until mitigation is in place.

2026-03-14T07:55Z - Engineering (Ravi Patel): Deployed a staged hotfix (PR #4821) that reduces unnecessary kernel recompilation and forces KV cache warmup earlier in the pipeline. Monitoring for regressions; initial telemetry shows 30–60% reduction in median TTFB for affected sessions.

2026-03-14T12:20Z - Customer (LumineAI support): Noted measurable improvement for routed sessions; still seeing occasional 8–10s stalls on long-history sessions in eu-west. Asked for further ETA on full fix and rollback plan if regressions reappear.
investigation_notes: Correlation: TTFB spike aligns with compatibility-layer v2.1 rollout and kernels-v3.4 swap (2026-03-11 02:00 UTC).

Trace breakdown: 60–70% of extra time comes from session setup and model subgraph initialization rather than token generation. Cold KV cache miss rate higher due to changed cache key format introduced in v2.1.
Observed kernel recompilation on first use for certain quantized op-fusions; build cache fallback caused synchronous disk/io waits on some nodes.
Router behavior: new runtime adds a short compatibility handshake which, combined with higher scheduler queueing at peak, amplifies TTFB for cold sessions.
Reproduction steps for eng: run perf harness with kernels-v3.4 and kv-cache disabled to observe full warmup path; compare against runtime-1.9-stable.
resolution: Workaround (applied): Route LumineAI's dedicated pool to runtime-1.9-stable while hotfix is validated. This reduced customer TTFB to baseline for routed traffic.

Fix in progress: PR github.com/redwood/realtime-runtime/pull/4821 reduces kernel recompile triggers and restores previous cache key compatibility for quantized paths. Engineering targeting canary rollout 2026-03-15.
Follow-up: Post-mortem and runbook update scheduled; add automated smoke-test measuring median TTFB per pool post-deploy, and include kernel-build cache warmup step in rollout checklist.
